meta.description: Maps metabolomics results to biological pathways via ORA, MSEA/QEA, mummichog/PSEA, and FELLA with explicit backgrounds and interpretive limits.
meta.note: final pass: fixed and audited under one brief, see CHECKPOINT.md

scientific_integrity.detail: All reported values come from fresh saved execution artifacts; no fabricated identifiers, clinical claims, or statistics were introduced.

practice_boundaries.detail: The Skill frames pathway mapping as research interpretation, rejects pool-size-to-flux claims, and does not diagnose or prescribe for individuals.

methodological_ground.detail: Fresh inputs confirmed explicit ORA backgrounds, full-table PSEA, deterministic seeding, and the documented distinction between predicted activity and metabolite identities.

code_usability.detail: All five shipped R scripts parsed. Fresh runs completed for mapping, local ORA, full-table PSEA, and FELLA; guarded failure cases exposed documented errors and emitted no result CSV.

functional_suitability.note: All promised entry points are present and primary local ORA, PSEA, and FELLA routes were freshly exercised. Literal NA output can overstate mapping coverage.

reliability.note: Expected invalid-table and API failures surface, but mummichog continues after validation and emits a secondary raw R error; literal NA is not rejected.

performance_context.note: Concise SKILL.md points to method-specific references and scripts; costly live dependencies are disclosed.

agent_usability.note: Decision table, input distinctions, failure modes, thresholds, and Common Errors support correct method selection.

human_usability.note: Natural triggers, clear usage strings, and strict scientific-input handling are appropriate under the Category-3 override.

security.note: Remote compound-list transfer and generic downloads are disclosed with a local default; mapping validation is incomplete.

maintainability.note: Final-pass references cleanly separate ORA, PSEA, and FELLA; all five scripts parse and have usage headers.

agent_specific.note: Progressive disclosure and integrations are clear; reruns can overwrite named outputs.

inputs.label: Map 12 identified metabolites and run Local-Only ORA with a 320-ID assay background
inputs.execution_note: Ran map_compounds.R then local_ora.R from the exact tip. Mapping was 12/12; hsa00020 p=9.372143e-11, FDR=3.327111e-09.
inputs.note: The default local route completed with a real KEGGREST table and explicit background.

assertions.text: Default ORA keeps user data local.
assertions.note: Only public KEGGREST reference data is fetched.

inputs.label: Run mummichog/PSEA twice on the full 1500-feature negative-mode table
inputs.execution_note: Ran mummichog_psea.R twice at 5 ppm, negative mode, p-cutoff 0.2, 200 permutations. Both CSVs have 15 rows and all.equal returned TRUE.
inputs.note: The full-table seeded PSEA workflow was deterministic.

inputs.label: Run PSEA on the 70-row significant-features-only table
inputs.execution_note: Ran mummichog_psea.R on the boundary file. It exited nonzero after logging 'There are too few m/z features' and wrote no result CSV.
inputs.note: It blocks an invalid, pre-enriched background; a secondary raw R error is a minor reliability issue.

inputs.label: Run FELLA diffusion on six TCA-associated KEGG IDs
inputs.execution_note: Ran fella_diffusion.R on cached hsa graph. It produced 206 rows; hsa00020 was top at p.score=7.400315e-06 and getExcluded returned character(0).

inputs.label: Interpret concentration enrichment with MSI-3 IDs and a hub-driven topology score
inputs.execution_note: Executed as Mode-A reasoning from exact Skill text: it requires MSI reporting, correct background, hub checks, and pool-versus-flux wording.

inputs.label: Map ten valid names plus one deliberately unknown name, then run Local-Only ORA
inputs.execution_note: Ran map_compounds.R and local_ora.R on a new 11-name file. It printed Mapped 11 of 11 but wrote ten KEGG IDs plus literal NA; ORA returned hsa00020 from real IDs.
inputs.note: New P1: literal NA makes mapping coverage unreliable.

assertions.text: Local ORA does not create a pathway hit from literal NA.
assertions.note: The real KEGG IDs drive the hsa00020 result.

inputs.label: Invoke the disclosed remote API path with a filtered background
inputs.execution_note: Ran ora_api.R. Live server returned documented errors 'Failed to connect to the API Server!' and 'Failed to perform pathway analysis!'; no output CSV was written. R status 2 appears as 2816 (0xB00) through Windows Git bash.
inputs.note: Known-failing remote alternative; working local default completed in Input 1.

key_strengths: All five shipped R scripts parsed, and mapping, Local-Only ORA, full-table PSEA, and FELLA were freshly executed at the exact tip.
Default ORA uses an assay background and returns a real TCA result without sending the compound list to the MetaboAnalyst API.
Two fresh full-table PSEA runs produced equal 15-row results under the documented seed.
The Skill applies appropriate ceilings around annotation uncertainty, backgrounds, topology hubs, and pool-versus-flux interpretation.

recommendations.title: Filter literal NA values before reporting or writing KEGG mappings
recommendations.problem: map_compounds.R retains the string NA for an unmapped compound, writes it to kegg_ids.txt, and reports it as mapped, making coverage misleading.
recommendations.root_cause: It filters R NA values but not literal text NA in the KEGG column.
recommendations.fix: Exclude both is.na(kegg_ids) and trimws(kegg_ids) == 'NA' before writing and counting mappings.

recommendations.title: Stop after failed mummichog validation
recommendations.problem: After the useful too-few-features error, the script calls SetPeakEnrichMethod on numeric 0 and emits a second raw R error.
recommendations.fix: Test whether mSet is numeric after validation; print current.msg and quit nonzero before later calls.
